      Lara has been missing since April 5th.  She was last seen at Sakura

   Park around 4 p.m. on that day. We are deeply concerned about her well-

      Please keep an eye out for Lara and share this notice with everyone you

   Color: Black

   Gender: Female

   Evening contact: Please TEXT Elaine Smith at 111-222-3333.

   Instead, please contact us immediately.

    We appreciate your help in spreading this information and keeping an

   eye out for Lara. We really hope she will come back home soon.

      Thank you for your kindness and support!

question: 解答番号21　英文を読み、空欄に入る最も適切なものを選びなさい。
explanation: 駅から学校へ歩く途中で、ペットボトルや缶などが道に散らばっていることに気付きました。
imageAltTexts:
公式問題 PDF 12ページ。
6  次の英文を読み，1 から4 の  　  内に入れるのに最も適当なものを，それぞれ1 ～4 のう

 ちから一つずつ選びなさい。解答番号は   21 ～   24  。



       Ken, a hardworking high school student, always took pride in his school and his role as a

  member of the student council.  Recently, as he was walking from the train station to school,

  he noticed that the street had become dirtier than before.  There were plastic bottles, cans,

  and even scraps of food scattered along the street. Ken felt he had to do something about this

   problem.  As he discussed the issue with friends at school, he found that many students

   shared his concern. This made him decide to take action.

      At the student council meeting, Ken proposed an idea of organizing a weekend clean-up

   event.  Initially, not everyone on the student council liked his plan. Some doubted whether it

  was worth the effort. They argued that the street would be clean for one day and then go

  back to being dirty again after a few days.  At the next meeting, however, he continued

   explaining the importance of this event. He argued that once the street became clean, those

   in the community would do their best to keep it clean.  In the end, all the members agreed to

   hold the event. A month before the clean-up, they put up posters about the event around the

   school and in nearby areas to gather students, teachers, and people from the community.

     On the day of the clean-up, Ken was pleasantly surprised to see so many people come out.

   Students, teachers, parents, and even local residents came with their gloves and trash bags to

   pick up garbage.  As they cleaned, they talked with each other about the school and

   community. Ken realized that cleaning up the street did not just make the school area look

   better; it also brought people together and built a sense of community among them.

     The clean-up event was a great success.  The street became clean again, and the

   participants felt a stronger connection to their school and community.  Ken felt a sense of

   accomplishment as a  leader.   This experience taught him that  positive changes  in the

  community begin with individuals who are determined to make a difference.

   event.  Initially, not everyone on the student council liked his plan. Some doubted whether it

  was worth the effort. They argued that the street would be clean for one day and then go

  back to being dirty again after a few days.  At the next meeting, however, he continued

   explaining the importance of this event. He argued that once the street became clean, those

   in the community would do their best to keep it clean.  In the end, all the members agreed to

   hold the event. A month before the clean-up, they put up posters about the event around the

   school and in nearby areas to gather students, teachers, and people from the community.

     On the day of the clean-up, Ken was pleasantly surprised to see so many people come out.

   Students, teachers, parents, and even local residents came with their gloves and trash bags to

   pick up garbage.  As they cleaned, they talked with each other about the school and

   community. Ken realized that cleaning up the street did not just make the school area look

   better; it also brought people together and built a sense of community among them.

     The clean-up event was a great success.  The street became clean again, and the

   participants felt a stronger connection to their school and community.  Ken felt a sense of

   accomplishment as a  leader.   This experience taught him that  positive changes  in the

  community begin with individuals who are determined to make a difference.
